decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with open gripper, lifting into elbow-up configuration while tilting down. Tube pose estimated from calibrated head RGB.
Advance left arm above the isolated left tube, continuing downward alignment without crossing the centerline.
Finish aligning the left gripper with the tube axis and descend toward the body; keep open until visual centering is checked.
Make millimeter centering correction, then close on the left tube body. Will verify retention during lift rather than relying on commanded gripper state.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table with a small backward retreat, maintaining tube alignment and elbow-up continuity.
Tube remains between the fingers after lifting. Carry it toward the left rack slot while rotating gradually upright; keep grip fully closed.
Continue controlled rotation toward upright and translate above the leftmost large rack opening. Leave clearance before insertion.
Finish upright alignment, then begin a slow vertical approach to the left rack opening. Check tube-to-hole centering before deep insertion.
Correct the tube a few millimeters toward the opening and lower vertically into the left rack slot while maintaining closed grip and upright orientation.
Fine-center over the left opening and gently complete the last insertion depth. Keep upright and closed until seating can be assessed.
Release the upright left tube at insertion height and withdraw the open fingers gently to inspect whether it remains seated in the rack.
Left tube remains upright in its slot after release. Retract the left arm while beginning an elbow-up, open-gripper approach to the inner right tube.
Continue right-arm descent alignment above the inner right tube, with smaller increments near the grasp. Return the empty left arm toward its origin.
Align the right fingers along the inner tube and descend to grasp height, staying open for a final visual check. Finish the left-arm return.
Make a small along-tube and yaw correction, then close the right fingers around the inner tube body. Keep the left arm parked.
Lift the inner right tube clear with the grip closed, retreating slightly before rotating upright. Inspect the next view for retention.
The right tube is retained after lifting. Carry inward above the rack and begin gradual upright rotation, keeping the right arm on its side and the grip closed.
Continue rotating the held tube toward vertical above the middle rack opening, with clearance from the already seated left tube.
Finish upright orientation and center the second tube above the middle slot, then approach vertically for a visual alignment check.
Fine-center the upright second tube over the middle opening and lower into the rack, keeping the grip closed until the insertion is checked.
Complete the last two centimeters of middle-slot insertion slowly, removing the small observed tilt before release.
The second cap has not descended as much as the wrist, suggesting contact at the opening. Make a small centering adjustment and gentle seating motion rather than forcing downward.
Open the right fingers to let the upright tube settle in the middle opening, then withdraw slowly and inspect its independent support.
The middle tube appears perched above the rack rather than fully seated. Regrasp and lift clear for a better hole-alignment view before retrying insertion.
The regrasp missed and the loose tube tilted across the rack. Open and align the right fingers to its new axis for a higher-body recovery grasp; avoid the seated left tube.
Move the open right fingers lower and toward the loose tube body using wrist-image centering. Recovery alignment remains uncertain, so approach in small increments.
The loose tube is lying along the rack rather than merely leaning upright. Lift and change to a downward recovery approach, keeping open and clear of the seated tube.
Replan from the executed single step after the continuity guard. Halve the lift and rotation increments to maintain the current elbow-up branch.
Continue the clear, downward recovery approach above the tube lying on the rack. Keep open and use conservative rotations through the current wrist configuration.
Move farther above the loose tube and continue aligning downward, using the wrist image to correct lateral centering without touching the rack.
Finish the downward recovery alignment and advance over the tube body on the rack, maintaining open fingers for a final centering view.
After the continuity interruption, avoid further forward rotation near the folded limit. Lower with very small increments at the observed orientation and close around the centered tube body.
Lift the recovered tube while retreating from the rack and easing out of the tightly folded pose. Begin upright rotation slowly and verify retention.
The recovered tube follows the gripper. Continue controlled upright rotation with clearance, repositioning over a free right-side opening before a new insertion attempt.
Finish upright rotation and position over the free right rack opening. Keep clearance so the tube axis and hole can be compared before descent.
Center the recovered upright tube over the rightmost large opening and descend vertically. Keep the grip closed and inspect for independent tube motion or rim contact.
The tube follows the descent without visible rim arrest. Continue slowly to seating height while preserving its upright alignment.
The tube shows some upward slip at the rim. Correct toward the front-row hole by about a centimeter without forcing down, then test a very small seating descent.
Release after the front-row centering adjustment and allow the tube to settle under gravity. Withdraw the fingers only slightly so its support and depth can be inspected.
The released tube fell toward the front instead of seating. Attempt to catch its body between the nearby fingers and lift clear for a corrected approach.
The tube is caught near its cap. Lift fully clear, then move back over the rack rather than the front edge; the higher grasp leaves room for a deeper insertion.
Lower the upright, high-grasped tube straight into the rightmost large opening. Compare tube motion with wrist motion before completing the depth.
Continue a slow vertical insertion from the higher grasp, checking that the tube remains upright and follows the gripper rather than sliding against a rim.
Rim contact is causing upward slip. Unload slightly, shift a few millimeters back and left toward the opening center, then gently test downward seating while keeping the tube captured.
Use the seated left tube and rack row direction to refine the right-slot center. Shift forward and slightly right, restoring vertical alignment, with only a shallow seating test.
Loosen the fingers slightly to guide rather than force the tube, and make a three-millimeter centering sweep so gravity can seat it if the opening is aligned.
Reclose and lift the tube clear of rim contact before another centering correction. Shift to the midpoint of the previous front/back tests, slightly left, rather than dragging against the plate.
Lower after unloading the rim and correct the tube's slight grasp-relative lean, estimated from its cap-to-tip head projection, to bring the tip under the cap.
The tube follows the corrected orientation without obvious slip. Continue the final slow vertical insertion, retaining the present alignment.
Open gradually without translating the wrist, allowing the nearly seated tube to settle while avoiding a withdrawal-induced tip. Inspect its independent position before moving away.
The tube is not independently seated and is tipping toward the fingers. Recapture and lift it clear; use a more central opening on the next attempt rather than continuing against the outer rim.
Lift and retreat well clear of the rack while retaining the caught tube. The cap obscures the wrist view, so inspect its free-space orientation before another placement.
